newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares move sideways on lack of impetus.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares move sideways on lack of impetus.

text.p: Hungarian shares moved sideways on Friday in the lack of factors showing a direction, with the market waiting for the first quarter 1997 earnings report of oil company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt MOL to be released on Tuesday, traders said.
According to preliminary figures, the BUX index finished at 5,880.92 points, dipping 0.63 points or 0.01 percent.
An official bourse statement said earlier on Friday that MOL would release its earnings reports with a delay from the May 15 deadline, on Tuesday, May 20.
MOL, the largest capitalised stock on the Budapest Stock Exchange, finished this week a global and a domestic offering of almost 20 percent of its shares.
Traders said the offerings have boosted the trade in MOL shares, and on Friday more than one million of the stocks changed hands on the BSE. MOL fell 25 forints to end at 3,370.

"There are two companies (brokerages) which push down the price," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities, adding that probably those investors were behind the deals who bought MOL shares at a discount price in the offerings and took profits on the BSE.
Traders said MOL's movements were likely to show direction to the BSE next week, while MOL's change was seen being determined mainly by the figures of the earnings report.
A decision in the U.S. next week to raise interest rates would weigh on Hungarian shares prices, traders added.
